ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: Name the artery that carries venous blood from the right ventricle of the heart to the lungs.
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: The image is a cross-sectional schematic diagram of the heart, where blue/purple large blood vessels can be seen extending from above the heart and branching toward the lungs, indicating an outflow pathway carrying venous blood; the ventricular region is in the lower part, and the right ventricle corresponds to the anatomical right side, the ventricle in the lower-left part of the image. Then reason: The question asks what the “artery” that transports venous blood from the right ventricle to the lungs is called. In the circulatory system, the blood vessel that arises from the right ventricle and sends deoxygenated blood to the lungs for gas exchange is the pulmonary artery.
